boundaries: No new allow rule, SELinux boolean, process domain, inode label or kernel policy was changed by these queries.
Query02 retained and re-evaluated the first147 rows exactly; the additional41 include one expected nonrequired null-device map denial.
System_r membership and valid contexts do not prove live service execution. The new profile must require strict SELinuxContext without an ignore-failure prefix and read back real process contexts.

The candidate service, systemd-run client, broker, PID1 and worker must have actual contexts and descriptor directions/labels verified. Merely checking a pipe read end does not prove the forwarded write end.

The two exact supported policy inputs in these offline helper files do not authorize treating a future independently modified policy as either old hash; future live helpers must pin that new input separately.

Direct QEMU was used with -I and -B. Only the two new private query prefixes and their private input copies received output. The sampled source root/dev/etc inode,mtime,ctime values did not change; this sampling is not a whole-rootfs content audit.
Both bounded foreground query processes ended with exit0; no query VM, PRoot job, mount or background process remains from this task.
